Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

**Testing symmetry in components**

I need to ensure that both the upper and lower parts of my design are symmetric across the center and that there's an empty boundary in the middle. I’m thinking of using a red line to separate the mirrored halves. It looks like the test components will involve the upper block (rows 1-3) and the lower bar (row 5), while row 4 serves as a separator. I'll need to program my test to create and run every pair, confirming that it correctly adds a red full row at row 4 before writing the file.

from pathlib import Path
base=Path('/home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-primeagentlearner-1792484937/attempts/902a26a1d741414098c8ca31bef93000/system/state/workspace/programs')
base.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
code='''def transform(grid):\n    out = [row[:] for row in grid]\n    # Mark the empty horizontal row separating the matching upper/lower shapes.\n    for r, row in enumerate(grid):\n        if all(v == 0 for v in row) and r > 0 and r + 1 < len(grid):\n            if any(any(v for v in x) for x in grid[:r]) and any(any(v for v in x) for x in grid[r+1:]):\n                out[r] = [3] * len(row)\n                break\n    return out\n'''
(base/'task-018df1b6.py').write_text(code)
